split_question: Should most convictions from childhood stop showing on job and college checks after a set number of years, apart from serious violent and sexual offences?
angles: Time limit: a fixed number of years, then the record drops off
Case by case: someone reviews each record before it is hidden
Keep disclosure, but help people explain it to employers
facts_for_writers: The proposals would not apply to serious violent and sexual offences; the minister for safeguarding said some convictions will always need to be disclosed. (s1)

Non-listed childhood convictions with custody of two years or less would stop being disclosed for life on standard and enhanced checks; the proposed filtering period is 11 years, double the current 5.5 years. (s2)
Between November 2023 and April 2026, 0.71% of 1.03 million standard checks and 0.35% of 10.31 million enhanced checks disclosed a childhood offence. (s2)
In a 2024 DWP employer survey, 47% of employers cited a criminal record as a barrier to hiring disadvantaged groups, the second most common barrier. (s2)
The Youth Justice Board's chief executive said checks serve public protection but continued disclosure can limit education and work that help rehabilitation. (s3)
